settings.label: Menu Acceleration
settings.help:
How quickly the list picks up speed when you hold a direction down.

A lower number gets moving sooner, which suits long lists. A higher number holds a steady pace for longer, which makes it easier to stop on the item you wanted.

Raise it if you keep overshooting.

settings.label: Activity Tracker
settings.help:
Records how long you play each item and how often you open it, which is what the Activity Tracker reads.

Turning it off stops anything new being recorded. Whatever has already been tracked is kept.

settings.label: Audio Subsystem Wait
settings.help:
Waits for the audio system to finish starting before showing the frontend.

Enable it if the first sound of the session is missed or cut short. Leaving it disabled provides the quickest boot.

settings.label: Audio Suspend
settings.help:
Lets the audio hardware power down when nothing is playing, which saves a little battery.

The cost is that the first moment of sound after a quiet spell can be clipped. Turn it off if you keep losing the start of sounds.

settings.label: Audio Reverse
settings.help:
Swaps the left and right channels over.

Only needed if your device or headphones have them the wrong way round, which you would notice as sound arriving from the opposite side to where it belongs.

settings.label: Box Art Padding Divisor
settings.help:
Box Art Padding in Customisation is a percentage, and this decides how much actual space each percent is worth.

A smaller number here makes every percent count for more, so the same padding setting pushes the artwork further from the edge. A larger number makes each percent count for less, so the padding becomes finer to adjust.

Leave it alone unless the padding steps feel too coarse or too gentle.

settings.label: Brightness On Boot
settings.help:
The screen brightness the device returns to each time it starts, whatever you had it set to before.

Handy if you tend to wind it right down at night and would rather not find it there in the morning.

settings.label: Raw Device Visibility
settings.help:
Shows nearby Bluetooth broadcasts that do not provide a useful device name.

These normally appear as a hardware address and are hidden to keep the scan list useful. Enable this only when diagnosing or pairing unusual hardware.

settings.label: Bluetooth Scan Timeout
settings.help:
How long the device keeps looking for nearby Bluetooth devices before giving up.

A longer scan picks up devices that are slow to announce themselves, a shorter one gets you back to the list sooner.

settings.label: Display Suspend
settings.help:
Lets the display power down properly when the device sleeps rather than simply going dark.

It saves a little battery, but some screens come back with flicker or no picture at all. If yours misbehaves after a sleep, turn this off.

settings.label: Double Buffering
settings.help:
Draws to a second full screen buffer instead of working with one.

This uses noticeably more memory and exists for comparing how things render, not for everyday use.

Leave it off unless you are chasing a display fault. Takes effect on the next launch.

settings.label: DPAD Swap Function
settings.help:
Lets the power button switch the DPAD between behaving normally and standing in for the sticks.

Handy for content that only reads one or the other. Leave it off if you would rather the power button did nothing else.

settings.label: Additional Cores
settings.help:
Shows the extra systems and cores in Core Assignment as well as the main ones.

Leave this off for a shorter list of the choices that suit most people. Content already assigned to an extra core keeps working either way.

settings.label: Font Source
settings.help: Select the font source: Language contains fonts for different writing systems, Theme uses fonts provided by the active theme, Internal contains the standard built-in fonts, and Custom contains your own font files.

settings.label: Brightness Increment
settings.help:
How far the brightness moves with each press.

A smaller step gives you finer control over the level, a larger one gets you from dim to bright in fewer presses.

settings.label: Volume Increment
settings.help:
How far the volume moves with each press.

A smaller step gives you finer control over the level, a larger one gets you from quiet to loud in fewer presses.

settings.label: LED During Play
settings.help:
Whether the power light stays lit while content is loading.

Purely cosmetic, and worth turning off if you would rather the light did not flash about while you are playing in the dark.

settings.label: Device Lid Switch
settings.help:
Whether closing the lid puts the device to sleep, on the devices that have one.

Turn it off if you would rather the lid did nothing at all.

settings.label: GPU Performance Mode
settings.help:
Holds the graphics chip at its top speed rather than letting it settle down when there is little to do.

It can smooth out the occasional stutter, at the cost of battery and a warmer device. Leave it off unless you have something that needs it.

settings.label: Overdrive
settings.help:
Raises the volume ceiling from 100% to 200%, for headphones or speakers that are simply too quiet.

Anything above 100% is pushing the output past what it was built for, so expect distortion and go up gently.

settings.label: Random Theme on Boot
settings.help:
Picks a different theme each time the device starts, chosen from the ones you have installed.

Leave it off if you would rather the theme you chose stayed put.

settings.label: Remember Section
settings.help:
Screens split into sections normally open on the first one. With this on they open wherever you last were.

Handy if you keep going back to the same section, less so if you would rather always start from the beginning.

settings.label: Menu Repeat Delay
settings.help:
How long a button must be held before it starts repeating.

A short delay means the list starts moving almost as soon as you press. A longer one lets you tap without the list running away from you.

Raise it if a single press sometimes moves you two places.

settings.label: RetroArch Startup Cache
settings.help:
Prepares part of RetroArch while the device starts so it opens faster the first time you use it.

This adds roughly three seconds to boot in exchange for a quicker first launch. Worth it if you play through RetroArch often, less so if you rarely do.

settings.label: RetroArch Network Wait
settings.help:
Holds RetroArch back until the device has joined a network.

Only worth having on if you rely on netplay or other online features the moment content opens. It adds a wait to every launch, so leave it off otherwise.

settings.label: Device Rumble
settings.help:
Whether the device gives a short buzz when it starts up, goes to sleep and shuts down.

This covers those three moments only. Content manages its own rumble separately.

settings.label: Stage Overlay
settings.help:
The small bars that slide in when you change brightness or volume, along with the battery warning.

Turn it off if you would rather nothing appeared over the top of what you are doing.

settings.label: Menu Navigation
settings.help:
Which controls move you around the menus, the DPAD, the sticks, or both together.

Set it to whichever you find yourself reaching for. On devices without sticks there is nothing here to change.

settings.label: System Swapfile
settings.help:
Sets aside space on your card for the device to fall back on when memory runs short.

A few demanding ports ask for this. It costs card space and is slower than real memory, so leave it alone unless something tells you otherwise.

settings.label: Thermal Zone Control
settings.help:
Lets the device shut itself down if it gets too hot.

This is a safety net rather than something you will meet in ordinary use. Leave it on, as turning it off means nothing will step in if the device runs hot.

settings.label: Trust Modifications
settings.help:
Settings screens normally ask whether to save when you leave with changes pending. With this on they simply save.

Quicker once you know your way around, though it does mean a change made by accident is kept without asking.

settings.label: Trust Power Choice
settings.help:
Rebooting and shutting down normally ask you to confirm first. With this on they happen straight away.

Quicker, but there is then nothing between a mistaken press and the device going down.

settings.label: Trust Removals
settings.help:
Removing content or resetting settings normally asks you to confirm first. With this on it happens straight away.

Worth thinking twice about, as there is no way back once something has been removed.

settings.label: USB Function
settings.help:
What the device offers when you plug it into a computer.

MTP lets you browse your files from the computer, which is what most people want. ADB is a developer connection and is only worth choosing if you know you need it.

settings.label: Verbose Messages
settings.help:
Shows the startup and shutdown messages scrolling past instead of the usual quiet screen.

Useful when something is going wrong at boot and you need to see where it stops. Leave it off otherwise.

settings.label: Volume On Boot
settings.help:
The volume the device returns to each time it starts, whatever you had it set to before.

Worth setting low if the device sometimes gets switched on somewhere quiet.

settings.label: System ZRam
settings.help:
Compressed memory held in RAM, giving you a little more to work with without touching your card.

Faster than the swapfile, though compressing costs a small amount of processing. Leave it alone unless something asks for it.

settings.label: Schedule
settings.help:
Warms the screen colours automatically on a sunrise and sunset schedule.

With this off, the single temperature below is used all day.

settings.label: Daytime / Manual Temperature
settings.help: The display temperature used during daytime when scheduling is enabled, or the manual display temperature when scheduling is disabled.

settings.label: Sunrise Time
settings.help: When the daytime temperature takes over.

settings.label: Sunset Temperature
settings.help:
The colour temperature used through the evening hours.

Higher is warmer and easier on the eyes at night.

settings.label: Sunset Time
settings.help: When the evening temperature takes over. Remember to go to bed at an appropriate time!

settings.label: Directory
settings.help: Choose which font directory to browse. This is available for language and custom fonts organised into folders.

settings.label: Face
settings.help:
Which style to use when a font file holds more than one, counted from 0.

Leave it at 0 unless the font calls for another style.

settings.label: Footer Size
settings.help:
The text size used in the footer bar.

Leave it at 0 to use whatever suits the device.

settings.label: Header Size
settings.help:
The text size used in the header bar.

Leave it at 0 to use whatever suits the device.

settings.label: Italic
settings.help: Use the italic axis provided by the selected variable font.

settings.label: List Size
settings.help:
The text size used for list items.

Leave it at 0 to use whatever suits the device.

settings.label: Name
settings.help: Choose which font or collection face to use from the selected font source.

settings.label: Panel Size
settings.help: Set the font size for grid panel labels (0 uses the device default, only applies in grid mode)

settings.label: Scale
settings.help:
Makes all text larger or smaller by the chosen amount, on top of the sizes set above.

This is what the Large Text accessibility profiles change.

settings.label: Width
settings.help: Adjust the width axis provided by the selected variable font.

settings.label: Background Music
settings.help:
Whether background music plays on the menus.

The music itself comes from your music folder.

settings.label: Background Music Volume
settings.help: How loud the background music is.

settings.label: Brightness
settings.help: Screen brightness as a percentage. Profiles retain the exact native 1-255 brightness level used by the device.

settings.label: Startup Chime
settings.help: Whether a short sound plays once the device has finished starting up.

settings.label: Language
settings.help:
Select your preferred language

Translations supported by Weblate

settings.label: Navigation Sound
settings.help: Whether the menus make a sound as you move through them.

settings.label: Sound Font
settings.help:
The soundfont used for General MIDI music, which decides how MIDI instruments sound.

Each soundfont can be previewed before you commit to it.

settings.label: Navigation Sound Volume
settings.help: How loud the navigation sounds are.

settings.label: Device Startup
settings.help:
Which screen the device opens on when it starts.

Content Collection opens the main Collections screen. Last Content always reopens the most recently launched content. Resume Content only reopens content after sleep shuts the device down.

settings.label: Theme Resolution
settings.help:
Draws the theme as though the screen were a different size.

Useful for trying a theme built for other hardware.

settings.label: Theme Scaling
settings.help:
How a theme built for another resolution is stretched or fitted to this screen.

Only comes into play once Theme Resolution has been changed.

settings.label: Timezone
settings.help: The region your device keeps time for. Setting this lets the clock correct itself from the internet, and handles daylight saving for you.

settings.label: Colour Depth
settings.help:
How many shades of each colour are sent.

Higher is smoother, though not every TV and cable will accept it.

settings.label: Mirror Output
settings.help:
Mirrors the HDMI output onto the device display, handy for live streaming.

Expect bars on the device display depending on the HDMI resolution selected.

settings.label: Colour Range
settings.help:
The range of brightness values sent.

If blacks look washed out or crushed, this is usually the setting at fault.

settings.label: Resolution
settings.help:
The resolution sent to the TV.

If no picture appears at all, try a lower one.

settings.label: Scan Scaling
settings.help:
Whether the picture is pushed out past the edges of the screen or pulled in from them.

Reach for this if the image is cut off or does not quite fill the screen.

settings.label: Colour Space
settings.help:
How colour is encoded on the way out.

RGB suits most TVs. Try the others only if the colours look plainly wrong.

settings.label: DPAD Swap Hotkey
settings.help: Which button combination switches the DPAD between behaving normally and standing in for the sticks.

settings.label: Screenshot Hotkey
settings.help: Which button combination takes a screenshot.

settings.label: Battery Alpha
settings.help: How strongly the low battery warning shows through.

settings.label: Battery Anchor
settings.help:
Where on the screen the low battery warning appears.

Worth moving if it lands over something you need to see.

settings.label: Battery Scale
settings.help: How large the low battery warning is drawn.

settings.label: Brightness Alpha
settings.help: How strongly the brightness indicator shows through.

settings.label: Brightness Anchor
settings.help: Where on the screen the brightness indicator appears.

settings.label: Brightness Scale
settings.help: How large the brightness indicator is drawn.

settings.label: General Alpha
settings.help:
How strongly the content overlay shows through.

Lower it if the overlay is fighting with the content underneath.

settings.label: General Anchor
settings.help: Where on the screen the content overlay sits.

settings.label: General Scale
settings.help: How large the content overlay is drawn.

settings.label: Volume Alpha
settings.help: How strongly the volume indicator shows through.

settings.label: Volume Anchor
settings.help: Where on the screen the volume indicator appears.

settings.label: Volume Scale
settings.help: How large the volume indicator is drawn.

settings.label: Idle Governor
settings.help:
How hard the processor works once the device has gone idle.

A gentler setting saves battery while nothing is happening. Leave it alone unless you are chasing battery life.

settings.label: Idle Display
settings.help:
How long the device sits without any input before dimming the screen.

Dimming saves battery without interrupting anything, and any press brings it straight back.

settings.label: Mute on Display Timeout
settings.help:
Whether sound is muted once the screen dims.

Handy if the device tends to dim while music is playing and you would rather it went quiet as well.

settings.label: Idle Sleep
settings.help:
How long the device sits without any input before going to sleep.

Sleep saves battery and picks up where you left off. Set it longer if it drops off while you are reading something.

settings.label: Low Battery
settings.help:
The capacity at which the red light comes on to tell you the battery is getting low.

Set it higher if you would rather have more warning.

settings.label: Saver Speed
settings.help:
How quickly the screensaver moves about.

Entirely a matter of taste.

How ludicrous!

settings.label: Saver Type
settings.help:
The screensaver shown once the screen has dimmed, or none at all.

This follows the Idle Display Timeout, so with that turned off you will never see one.

settings.label: Shutdown
settings.help:
What a short press of the power button does, whether that is sleeping, shutting down, or nothing at all.

Holding the button down shuts the device off regardless.

settings.label: Content Item Count
settings.help: Override the number of visible list items (0 uses the theme default)

settings.label: Footer Height
settings.help: Override the theme footer bar height in pixels (Default uses the theme value)

settings.label: Glyph Size Footer
settings.help: Override the footer glyph render size in pixels (Default uses the theme value, Auto fits to item height, Native uses the actual size)

settings.label: Glyph Size Grid
settings.help: Override the grid glyph render size in pixels (Default uses the theme value, Auto fits to the cell, Native uses the actual size)

settings.label: Glyph Size Header
settings.help: Override the header glyph render size in pixels (Default uses the theme value, Auto fits to header height, Native uses the actual size)

settings.label: Glyph Size List
settings.help: Override the list glyph render size in pixels (Default uses the theme value, Auto fits to item height, Native uses the actual size)

settings.label: Header Height
settings.help: Override the theme header bar height in pixels (Default uses the theme value)

settings.label: Label Width
settings.help: Override the maximum width of the left side option label as a percentage of content width (Default uses the theme value)

settings.label: Background Scale
settings.help: How the wallpaper is fitted to the screen, whether stretched, cropped or left as it is.

settings.label: Battery
settings.help: How the battery appears in the header, as a glyph, a percentage or both, or hidden altogether.

settings.label: Black Fade Animation
settings.help: Whether the screen fades out to black as content launches, rather than cutting straight across.

settings.label: Bluetooth
settings.help: Whether the Bluetooth indicator appears in the header.

settings.label: Bold Focus
settings.help: Draws a thicker marker around the highlighted item, so you can tell at a glance where you are in a list.

settings.label: Box Art
settings.help:
Which artwork is preferred when a piece of content has more than one image to choose from.

The first kind that exists for an item is the one you will see.

settings.label: Box Art Alignment
settings.help:
Where the artwork sits on the screen.

Worth pairing with whichever side your theme leaves free.

settings.label: Hide Box Art
settings.help:
Whether system artwork appears in Content Explorer while grid mode is on.

Turn it off if you would rather see plain names in the grid.

settings.label: Box Art Padding
settings.help:
Breathing room around the artwork on all sides, as a percentage.

If the steps feel too coarse or too gentle, Box Art Padding Divisor in Advanced changes what each percent is worth.

settings.label: Box Art Placeholder
settings.help:
Shows the theme's stand in image when an item has no artwork of its own.

Turn it off if you would rather have empty space than a placeholder.

settings.label: Box Art Scale
settings.help:
How much of the space available the artwork fills, as a percentage.

Lower it if the artwork is crowding out the list.

settings.label: Box Art Transition
settings.help: How the artwork arrives as you move through the list, whether that is a fade, a slide, or nothing at all.

settings.label: Clock
settings.help: Whether the time appears in the header.

settings.label: Collection In Content
settings.help: Whether your collections appear inside Content Explorer as well as on their own screen.

settings.label: History In Content
settings.help: Whether your recent history appears inside Content Explorer as well as on its own screen.

settings.label: Full Width Selection
settings.help: Whether the highlight behind the selected item runs the full width of the screen or stops short of it.

settings.label: Menu Counter File
settings.help: Toggle the visibility of currently selected file along with total in Explore Content

settings.label: Menu Counter Folder
settings.help: Toggle the visibility of currently selected folder along with total in Explore Content

settings.label: Dash to Colon
settings.help: Show a colon instead of a dash in content names, which often reads a little cleaner

settings.label: Element Transition
settings.help: Select the animation used when dialogues, toast messages and help boxes appear

settings.label: Empty Folders
settings.help:
Whether folders with nothing in them are still listed.

Hiding them tidies up a card with plenty of unused system folders.

settings.label: Folder Item Count
settings.help: Whether folders show how many items are inside them.

settings.label: Forward History
settings.help:
Whether coming back out of a folder returns you to the item you went in on.

Saves scrolling back down a long list every time.

settings.label: Friendly Folder Names
settings.help: Replaces the label of shortened content folders to more appropriately named labels

settings.label: Grid Mode Content
settings.help: Lets content be shown as a grid of artwork rather than a list of names, on themes built to support it.

settings.label: Group Content Items
settings.help: Gather content into folders by starting letter, either one letter each or several letters together, with numbers kept separate

settings.label: Screen Title
settings.help: Whether the name of the current screen appears along the top.

settings.label: Show Hidden Content
settings.help: Toggle hidden content displayed in Explore Content - Place a '.' or '_' character at the start of a file or folder name to hide it

settings.label: High Contrast
settings.help: Uses plain, strongly contrasting colours whatever theme is active, so text stands clearly apart from what is behind it.

settings.label: Label Scroll Speed
settings.help: Controls the scroll speed for labels - Disabled turns off all scrolling, Slow and Fast adjust the animation speed with proportional pause durations

settings.label: Save State Launch
settings.help:
Whether pressing A picks up from your last save state, or whether holding A is what does that.

Set it to whichever you find yourself doing more often.

settings.label: Launch Splash
settings.help:
Shows content artwork while the content starts. Splash catalogues can use still images, animated GIF, WebP or APNG images, and MP4 video.

A number of seconds keeps the splash up for at least that long. Until Finished plays animations and videos through once, and keeps still images up until a button is pressed. Until Button Press keeps any splash up until a button is pressed.

settings.label: List Glyph
settings.help: Toggle icon glyphs for menu and content list items - does not affect header, footer, grid or carousel glyphs

settings.label: Mixed Folder Content
settings.help: If enabled folders within content explorer will be mixed in with other content alphabetically

settings.label: Remove Bracketed Text
settings.help: Remove extra information from content labels - This does NOT rename your files it only changes how it is displayed

settings.label: Label Scroll Style
settings.help: Controls how labels scroll when they exceed half the display width - Disabled stops all scrolling, Continuous loops indefinitely, Bounce scrolls to the end then returns

settings.label: Network
settings.help:
Whether the Wi-Fi indicator appears in the header.

Its strength reflects the local wireless link and does not claim that the Internet is reachable.

settings.label: Message Duration
settings.help: How long a passing message stays on screen before the next one takes its place.

settings.label: Overlay Image
settings.help:
An image laid over the frontend, usually to imitate a screen grille or add a border.

This covers the menus only, not your content.

settings.label: Overlay Transparency
settings.help:
How strongly the frontend overlay shows through.

Lower it if the overlay is fighting with what is underneath.

settings.label: Shoulder Button Skip
settings.help:
Choose whether the shoulder buttons move a page at a time or jump to the next starting letter

Letter jumping needs an alphabetical sort order, so any other sort falls back to moving a page at a time

settings.label: Startup Messages
settings.help: Show or hide Pickles content start-up and RetroAchievements connection messages

settings.label: Power Effects
settings.help: Collapse the content picture like an old television when leaving Pickles or Wasabi, and open it back up when content starts after a launch splash. Reduce Motion disables these effects.

settings.label: Reduce Motion
settings.help: Reduced swaps sliding and bouncing for gentle fades. Maximum removes transitions and moving elements altogether.

settings.label: Save Screenshot
settings.help:
Shows your most recent save picture in place of the box art for anything played through Pickles.

Items you have not saved yet keep their usual artwork.

settings.label: Selection Intensity
settings.help: Controls the intensity of the selection animation when navigating between list and grid items

settings.label: Selection Direction
settings.help: Controls the style of the selection animation applied when navigating between list and grid items

settings.label: Shadow Rendering
settings.help: A soft shadow behind list text and glyphs, which helps them stand off a busy wallpaper.

settings.label: Shuffle Function
settings.help:
Lets R2 throw you at a random item in the current list.

Handy when you cannot decide what to play.

settings.label: Sort Order
settings.help: Whether the current sort order is shown in the header, which saves opening the menu to check.

settings.label: Tag Order
settings.help: Whether an item's tag glyph is shown beside it.

settings.label: Move Leading The
settings.help: Move a trailing 'The' back to the front of a name, so 'Batman and Robin, The' reads as 'The Batman and Robin'

settings.label: Title Include Root Drive
settings.help: Changes the top title label in Explore Content to show current storage device along with folder name

settings.label: Video Wallpaper
settings.help:
Plays the theme's video wallpaper behind the menus, where the theme provides one.

It costs a little battery, so turn it off if you would rather keep that.

settings.label: Web Dashboard
settings.help: A home page in the browser showing what the device is doing, with activity, system information, remote viewing, playback controls, and device tools.

settings.label: Web Dashboard Authentication
settings.help:
Whether changes made through the Web Dashboard need a code.

Disabled, anyone on your network can manage files, save from Editors and Tools, change History and Collections, and control Wasabi and Pickles without a code. Enabled, changes require the code from Web Dashboard Code.

settings.label: Web Dashboard Port
settings.help:
The port used to reach this service from a web browser.

Change it only if something else is already using that port.

settings.label: Live View FPS
settings.help:
How many pictures a second Live Remote View sends, from 5 to 60 in steps of 5.

Higher is smoother but uses more processing on the device and more of your network, and the device may not reach the rate it is asked for. 15 is the default.

settings.label: Live View Quality
settings.help:
How sharp each Live Remote View picture is, from 20 to 100 in steps of 5.

Higher is clearer but sends more data for every picture. 70 is the default.

settings.label: Local DNS Resolver
settings.help:
Makes the device available at a memorable .local address without changing its system hostname.

Use a different local name when more than one muOS device shares a network.

settings.label: Local Name
settings.help:
The address used before .local in a browser.

For example, muos becomes muos.local. This does not alter the device hostname.

settings.label: Remote Controls
settings.help:
Whether Remote View shows buttons, volume and brightness controls that work the device from the browser. Enabled with Sticks also adds the analogue sticks, on devices that have them, and lets a game controller connected to the browser move them.

They need Authentication and the code from Web Dashboard Code, because anyone using them can do anything you can do with the device in your hands. With Authentication and Remote View Privacy both disabled, they are open to anyone on your network, but only while Remote View is set to Live.

settings.label: Remote View Privacy
settings.help:
Whether Remote View protects what is on the screen.

Enabled, Remote View needs the code from Web Dashboard Code and never captures private screens such as Web Dashboard Code, passcodes and passwords. Disabled, anyone on your network can open Remote View without unlocking and every screen is captured, including the Web Dashboard Code, which lets them unlock the dashboard too.

settings.label: Remote View
settings.help:
How often the Web Dashboard may take a picture of the screen for Remote View. Live streams the screen as it changes, at the rate set by Live View FPS. Manual only takes a picture when you press Refresh now in the dashboard, so the picture never changes while you are looking at it.

Remote View needs Authentication and the code from Web Dashboard Code. The screen is only captured while someone is watching, and never while a private screen such as Web Dashboard Code is open. Live uses more processing and network while it is open. Disabled hides Remote View from the dashboard.

settings.label: Secure File Transfer
settings.help: Root-backed file transfer for your storage, the boot partition and MustardOS itself. Enabling it grants read and write access to those locations. Connect on port 2022 with the username muos and password muos.

settings.label: Secure File Transfer Port
settings.help:
The network port this service listens on.

The default suits almost everyone. Change it only if something else is already using that port.

settings.label: Secure Shell
settings.help: Root command-line access through Secure Shell.

settings.label: Secure Shell Port
settings.help:
The network port this service listens on.

The default suits almost everyone. Change it only if something else is already using that port.

settings.label: Syncthing
settings.help: Keeps folders in step with another machine over the network.

settings.label: Syncthing Web Port
settings.help:
The port used to reach this service from a web browser.

Change it only if something else is already using that port.

settings.label: Virtual Terminal
settings.help:
Whether this service runs.

Each one costs a little battery and memory while it is on, so leave off what you do not use.

settings.label: Virtual Terminal Port
settings.help:
The network port this service listens on.

The default suits almost everyone. Change it only if something else is already using that port.

wifi.name: pass
wifi.label: Password, leave it empty for an open network

wifi.name: type
wifi.label: dhcp to be given an address automatically, or static to set one yourself

wifi.name: subnet
wifi.label: Static subnet prefix length, such as 24

wifi.name: proxy_noproxy
wifi.label: Addresses that skip the proxy, separated by commas

builtin.name: Clear View
builtin.description: Slightly larger text in an easy to read typeface, with a stronger highlight on the selected item

builtin.name: Low Vision
builtin.description: Larger text, strong contrast and a legible typeface, with messages and scrolling labels that stay on screen longer

builtin.name: Large Print
builtin.description: The largest text with strong contrast and a legible typeface, and box art turned off so lists have room to breathe

builtin.name: Calm Motion
